Independent bounded test: enumerate every length-n four-color word with weight the product of (2+3 times prior count of its next color), divide by product_{k=0}^{n-1}(8+3k), and accumulate the two statistics and their product
correctness.rationale: The sequence probability is exchangeable and the distinguished color's occupancy is beta-binomial. Conditional on that color's count r, its positions are uniform and the others, in order, have the (q-1)-color symmetric urn law. For any adjacent pair the conditional change probability splits into exactly one distinguished position and two others; multiplying by n-1 gives the two terms of (6). Subtraction of the unconditional (n-1)d_q and symmetry give (1), also when n-r is 0 or 1 or q=2. Independently, conditioning on the complete occupancy vector yields E[R_n|N]=(n^2-sum_j N_j^2)/n, and the second factorial moments of the remaining occupancies give the same expression. Writing D=qa+1, E=(q-1)a+1, the leading coefficient b-d is -a(a+1)/(DE); F(r) is strictly negative for r>=2 while F(qr)=r(a+r)(q-1)(qa+2)/(DE)>0. Concavity and the negative limit at infinity prove the ordered roots and exact integer classification. For r=1, F(n)=(n-1)(a+1)/E times (2-na/D). For r large, scaling x=tr gives limiting quadratic -(d-b)t^2+2(1-b)t-(2-b) with an affine O(1/r) correction. Its center is D/a and squared half-width is DE/[a^2(a+1)], verifying (3); strict signs at 1,q and infinity ensure simple roots and the O(1) location error in n. Direct sequential-weight enumeration at q=4,a=2/3,n=2..6 independently agreed for all 20 frequencies, within 6e-16 in the covariance.
residual_risks: Integer zeros occur only for roots on the integer lattice. The proof and finite test are not for asymmetric urns or unequal reinforcements; the large-r statement holds with q and a fixed.
